criteria.name: Identity and official footprint
criteria.assessment: GIS FID 825 identifies Gemini, COOP, 172 Littleton St. The reopened slab reproduces the 14-vertex GIS outline at the local centroid; this checks the slab ring, not necessarily every facade wall or master placement.

criteria.name: Scale and placement
criteria.assessment: Metric units and centroid-local geometry are evident, and the footprint vertex agreement supports plan scale. Roof elevations, storey heights, and campus marker placement have no independent surveyed or master-scene validation in this standalone asset review.

evidence.placement_source: manifest/master placement not independently reopened in this isolated-asset grading

criteria.name: Roof form and height evidence
criteria.assessment: Multiple ranges, two front cross-gables, dormer elements, and three chimney masses create a more articulated silhouette than a simple bar. Against the official oblique image, the main roof still reads as a broad continuous gable with thin, schematic intersections; dormers are shallow block forms. Ridge/chimney elevations are estimates, not measured evidence.

evidence.height_status: estimated from photo; no surveyed elevation

criteria.name: Facade and entrance
criteria.assessment: Dark brick base, light siding, windows, and a covered entry evoke the official house. The reference facade has strongly differentiated wings, an asymmetrical opening rhythm, a substantial recessed porch with a continuous railing and broad approach. The asset facade remains repetitive, porch details are comparatively minimal, and roof gable faces/window rhythm do not fully follow the photo.

evidence.photo: current official exterior photo showing brick lower story, cream siding, multiple projecting gables, dormers, and deep center porch

criteria.name: Materials, interior, and portability
criteria.assessment: Named brick, siding, roof, trim, glazing, and interior materials support the intended look. The interior contains floor plates, corridor/room partitions, and a few common-room props but is schematic and visually not verified as an as-built plan. Fresh-open structure is self-contained without linked libraries or unpacked image dependencies.

source_evidence.measurement_method: Official GIS lon/lat polygon transformed using project approximate local conversion; vertex comparison on reopened slab XY; 3D extent from mesh world coordinates; visual comparison against current official exterior image.
source_evidence.uncertainty: Approximate GIS conversion; no survey, measured elevations, authoritative plans, or master placement validation.

findings: Official FID 825 wall-outline candidate matches the slab XY ring to rounding precision; walls may be offset from a GIS polygon and this does not validate the master placement.
The current official photo visibly supports a multi-wing house with a deep central porch, brick lower facade, pale siding, intersecting gables, dormers, and chimney stacks.
Asset materials and three-level schematic content are useful, but no reliable interior plan or surveyed height was available; the GIS record's NUM_LEVELS=1 remains conflicting, ambiguous source data.
Portability is strong on fresh open: no linked libraries or unpacked external image dependencies were found.
required_fixes_if_below_8: Reshape the roof silhouette to match the photo's distinct stepped wings and deeper intersecting gables/valleys, preserving the GIS wall footprint; support heights with a measured elevation or keep the dimensions explicitly estimated.
Rework the front composition around the image-visible center porch: deeper/recessed entry, continuous rail line and broad stair/landing; shift and vary facade windows to match the separate wings.
Model dormers with clear pitched caps/cheeks and vary their sizes and spacing to match the current photo rather than using shallow box faces.
Retain interior as schematic unless a trustworthy floor plan is found; add clear floor/cutaway review evidence if interior usability is a goal.
